body_markdown:
The sweaters are coming out, pumpkin-spiced everything is back, and somehow the end of the year is already in sight.


For commercial real estate (CRE) teams, fall is more than a seasonal shift. It’s a critical opportunity to step back from the day-to-day and look ahead. Q4 brings year-end deadlines, budget planning, portfolio reviews, staffing decisions, and the opportunity to set the stage for a stronger year ahead.


But strategic planning doesn’t have to mean disappearing into a conference room for three days with a stack of spreadsheets. The best Q4 planning starts with a simple question:


*What do we need to know, fix, or change now to make next year better?*


##


**The CRE Guide to Q4**


###


**Look Back Before You Look Ahead**


Before building next year’s strategy, take an honest look at what happened this year. What worked well? What fell short? And where were opportunities missed?


Review performance across the areas that matter most to your portfolio, from occupancy and leasing activity to tenant retention, operating expenses, and overall asset performance. The goal isn’t to dwell on what went wrong—it’s to identify patterns and understand what they’re telling you.


If the same challenge surfaced repeatedly throughout the year, Q4 is the time to ask what needs to change. Maybe the answer is a better process, additional resources, new technology, or simply a different approach. Whatever the solution, identifying it now gives your team a chance to build it into next year’s strategy.


###


**Take a Hard Look at Your Team**


A strategic plan is only as effective as the team responsible for executing it. Q4 is an ideal time to evaluate whether your current staffing structure matches your 2027 goals. Are your teams spending their time on high-value work, or are they buried in administrative tasks and repetitive processes?


Consider where your team has capacity and where it doesn’t. You may find that you don’t necessarily need to hire more full-time employees. You may need additional expertise during peak periods, specialized support for specific projects, or a more flexible staffing model that can scale with demand.


[Strategic staffing](https://propmgtdiv.bgsf.com/) can help CRE teams put the right resources in the right places without automatically adding permanent overhead.


###


**Review the Work Behind the Work**


Sometimes the biggest opportunities aren’t found in major strategic initiatives. They’re hiding in everyday processes.


How many hours are spent building reports? Are different departments working from different versions of the same data? Are employees spending more time searching for information than acting on it?


Q4 is a great time to identify these operational inefficiencies. Look for processes that are:


-


Repetitive


-


Manual


-


Time-consuming


-


Prone to errors


-


Dependent on one person


-


Difficult to scale


Then ask:


*Does this really need to be done the way we’re doing it?*


###


**Make Technology Part of the Strategy**


Technology should do more than give your team another login. As CRE organizations evaluate their technology stacks, Q4 is a good time to determine whether existing tools are actually solving problems or simply adding complexity.


Review the systems your teams rely on for property management, accounting, reporting, maintenance, etc. Ask your team what they love, what they tolerate, and what they wish worked differently.


You may discover that the answer isn’t always another platform. Sometimes the bigger opportunity is improving how existing technology is implemented, integrated, or used.


###


**Get Serious About Data**


Strategic planning starts with having the right information at the right time. When leadership can’t quickly access accurate, consistent data, it becomes harder to make confident decisions about budgets, staffing, investments, and portfolio performance.


Use Q4 as an opportunity to identify gaps in your reporting and data processes. Do you have a clear picture of performance across your properties? Are teams working from consistent metrics? Can leadership quickly spot trends and turn insights into action?


The goal is simple: spend less time collecting, comparing, and reconciling information—and more time using it to make smarter decisions.


###


**Plan for the Unexpected**


If the last few years have taught CRE anything, it’s that flexibility matters.


Your Q4 plan shouldn’t assume that everything will go exactly according to schedule. Build room for changing market conditions, unexpected vacancies, staffing challenges, shifting tenant needs, and other variables.


Consider where your organization is most vulnerable to disruption and identify contingency plans before you need them. That might mean developing backup staffing resources, cross-training employees, documenting critical processes, or identifying outside partners who can step in when internal teams reach capacity.


The best strategic plans aren’t rigid. They give teams a framework for responding when circumstances change.


##


**Turn Q4 Into a Launchpad for 2027**


Sweater weather may signal the approach of the holidays, but for CRE leaders, fall should also signal


*planning season* . Before Q4 gets swallowed by year-end reporting, budgets, deadlines, and holiday schedules, carve out time to look at the bigger picture. Evaluate performance, examine processes, listen to your team, review your technology, and identify resource gaps. Most importantly, establish clear priorities for 2027, assign ownership, determine the resources you’ll need, and build realistic timelines for getting there.


The goal is to enter the new year with a clear path to action. Your team should understand what you’re doing, why you’re doing it, who owns it, what resources are needed, and how you’ll measure success. Because the best time to prepare for next year isn’t January 1. It’s now.


Identify your staffing gaps, strengthen your team, and start the new year with the resources you need to execute your strategy.
